from.place: Proof, final sentence: 'A cover preserving functor that preserves compatible families is continuous.'

title: Cover- and compatible-preserving functors are continuous
statement: Let $C,D$ be categories with Grothendieck topologies $J,K$, and let $F:C\to D$ be a functor. Assume that $F$ is cover-preserving: for every $J$-covering sieve $R$ on $c$, the sieve generated by all $F(r)$, $r\in R$, is $K$-covering on $F(c)$. Assume also that $F$ is compatible-preserving: for every set-valued $K$-sheaf $P$, every presieve $T$ on $z\in C$, every compatible family $x$ of $F^{\mathrm{op}}P$ on $T$, and every $g_i:y_i\to z$ in $T$ and $f_i:w\to F(y_i)$ satisfying $F(g_1)f_1=F(g_2)f_2$, one has $P(f_1)(x_{g_1})=P(f_2)(x_{g_2})$. Then $F$ is continuous: for every set-valued $K$-sheaf $P$, the presheaf $F^{\mathrm{op}}P$ is a $J$-sheaf. Here presheaves of sets are contravariant functors to sets, in the convention of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1).

CoverPreserving and CompatiblePreserving are spelled out as in lines 58-59 and 81-86 of that file. Functor.IsContinuous is precisely preservation of sheaves under precomposition (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Continuous.lean:197-198). The compatibility hypothesis is taken for all set universes, so in particular for the universe required by the criterion.
